name: Merkel Cell Carcinoma
aliases: Primary neuroendocrine carcinoma of the skin

criteria.description: Histopathologic identification of small round blue cells with neuroendocrine features
Positive staining for cytokeratin 20 in a perinuclear dot pattern
Rapidly growing, painless, firm, red to violaceous nodule on sun-exposed skin
Detection of Merkel cell polyomavirus DNA in tumor tissue (supportive)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic histopathology and immunohistochemistry findings combined with compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires biopsy with immunohistochemical confirmation; MCPyV detection supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.

occasional.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as weight loss

rare.symptomName: Respiratory symptoms due to lung metastases

laboratory: Elevated serum neuron-specific enolase (NSE) in some cases
imaging: CT or MRI showing local tumor extent and lymph node involvement
PET scan for detection of metastases
genetic: Presence of Merkel cell polyomavirus DNA in tumor cells (in ~80% of cases)
other: Immunohistochemistry positive for cytokeratin 20 (CK20) with perinuclear dot pattern
Positive staining for neuroendocrine markers (chromogranin, synaptophysin)

distinguishingFeatures: Primary lung origin with pulmonary symptoms
Different immunohistochemical profile (CK20 negative, TTF-1 positive)
Positive staining for S100 and HMB-45
Slower growth compared to Merkel cell carcinoma

redFlags: New onset of systemic symptoms such as weight loss or fatigue
references: Harms PW, et al. The biology and treatment of Merkel cell carcinoma: current understanding and future directions. Nat Rev Clin Oncol. 2018.
Paulson KG, et al. Merkel cell carcinoma: current US incidence and projected increases based on changing demographics. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2018.
Toker C. Trabecular carcinoma of the skin. Arch Dermatol. 1972.
